cards.explanation: The answer is in his own house. David says, "I will walk in my house with integrity of heart." Anybody can look holy at a crowded event, friends. Your own house is where nobody is clapping. I think David started there on purpose.

The answer is that he hates it and it won't cling to him. David says, "I hate the work of those who fall away; it shall not cling to me." He's not just avoiding it, friends, he says he hates it. And he says it shall not cling to him, so he wants none of it stuck on him.
The answer is evil. David says, "I will know nothing of evil." He's saying he won't get familiar with it, friends. I think that's a pretty big promise to make out loud.

The answer is that he'll put them to silence. David says, "Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, I will put to silence…" Slander in secret is the kind that hides, and David says he'll shut it down. The verse gives no steps in between, friends.

The answer is True. David says, "the one with haughty eyes and a proud heart, I will not endure." Haughty eyes look down on other people, and a proud heart is that same pride on the inside. David names both together, friends, and he says he won't put up with that person.

The answer is the faithful of the land. David says, "My eyes favor the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me…" His eyes favor them, friends. The faithful are the ones he says may dwell with him.

The answer is minister. David says, "he who walks in the way of integrity shall minister to me." Walking in integrity is what he's looking for in the people who serve him. Notice, friends, it's the same word, integrity, that he used for himself in verse 2 (Psalm 101:2).

The answer is False. David says, "No one who practices deceit shall dwell in my house; no one who tells lies shall stand in my presence." So deceit doesn't get to move in, friends. Lying doesn't get to stand in front of him either.

The answer is every morning. David says, "Every morning I will remove all the wicked of the land…" Every morning, friends, not once in a while. I set my timer for a lot of things, but I'd have a hard time keeping up with this one.

The answer is False. David starts with his house (Psalm 101:2), but the last verse reaches out, friends. David says, "Every morning I will remove all the wicked of the land…" and "…every evildoer from the city of the LORD." The land and the city are a lot more than one house.
